`imbue/minds_evals/templates/` is type-checked. Those files run inside the verifier container rather than the dev process, and two of them (`tests/gates/checks.py`, `tests/quality/wordiness.py`) import `rewardkit`, which the container installs via `uvx` -- so the whole directory was excluded from this project's `ty` config and checked nowhere. The other three are pure stdlib and were excluded only by association, including `tests/finalize.py`, which composes every trial's final gated reward.

`harbor-rewardkit` joins the dev group so the type checker can resolve those imports. Nothing this project runs imports it; it exists for the checker alone, which is exactly what makes it easy to prune as unused. Two checks in `imbue/minds_evals/typecheck_coverage_test.py` hold it in place: `templates/` must stay un-excluded with rewardkit declared, and the dev-group pin must equal the one `templates/tests/test.sh` passes to `uvx`, so the version being checked is the version that grades trials.

This covers import and signature drift across those files, not their behaviour. The wiring they sit in -- `judge.toml`, `reward.toml`, `test.sh` ordering, the verifier Dockerfile -- is still only exercised by a real trial.
